source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer:
STANCE 21 - Speculative decoding changes the economics of the fix: measure redundancy cost in accepted-token terms, not wall-clock turns.
Mechanism. On a fleet running speculative decoding, a redundant tool call does not cost one turn of decode at the naive rate. It costs one extra prefill of the grown context plus a decode segment whose effective throughput depends on the draft acceptance rate. Tool-result tokens are structured and highly predictable, so the draft model typically accepts them at a higher rate than free-form prose; the marginal cost of the redundant turn is therefore lower than a turn-count metric implies, while the prefill cost of the longer context is higher than it implies.
Falsifiable hypothesis H21. Cost per redundant call expressed in GPU-seconds is dominated by re-prefill of the accumulated context, not by decode, once context exceeds a few thousand tokens. If measured decode GPU-seconds exceed prefill GPU-seconds for the redundant segment, H21 is refuted and the fix should target decode length instead of turn count.
Metrics. Per-redundant-call: prefill tokens, cached prefix hit fraction, decode tokens, draft acceptance rate on tool-result spans versus prose spans, GPU-seconds attributed by phase, and end-to-end added latency at p50/p95.
Controlled experiment. Replay a fixed trajectory set through the serving stack twice: Arm A with the redundant call present, Arm B with the call elided from the replay. Identical weights, identical seeds, identical batch composition and concurrency. Paired per-item deltas. Run each arm three times and report variance, because acceptance rate is sensitive to batch composition.
Boundary conditions. Prefix caching invalidates this analysis if it is enabled and hitting, since the re-prefill may be nearly free; report the cache hit fraction alongside every number or the result is uninterpretable. Chunked prefill also shifts the phase attribution.
Confounders. Acceptance rate co-varies with batch size, so any throughput delta between arms may be a batching artifact rather than a redundancy effect. Continuous batching means the two arms do not see identical neighbors unless the replay is run at fixed concurrency with a fixed request mix.
Numbers. No figure here is MEASURED. The claim that prefill dominates past a few thousand tokens is an ESTIMATE derived from the fact that prefill is compute-bound and scales with context length while incremental decode is memory-bandwidth-bound and scales with generated tokens; it must be confirmed on this fleet before it is quoted.
Rollback. This is a measurement task, not a deployment, so the rollback gate is on the conclusion: if the phase-attribution variance across the three repeats exceeds 15% relative, discard the numbers rather than publishing them.
Scope. This is a serving-system measurement. It quantifies what redundancy costs on this hardware and says nothing about whether the model knows when to abstain.
risks: Prefix caching or chunked prefill can make the phase attribution meaningless if their state is not reported
Draft acceptance rate co-varies with batch composition, so throughput deltas may be batching artifacts
Replaying elided trajectories assumes the elision is behaviorally neutral, which is exactly what is in question
evidence_required: Phase-attributed GPU-seconds table with prefix-cache hit fraction per arm
Draft acceptance rate broken out for tool-result spans versus prose spans
Three-repeat variance report at fixed concurrency and fixed request mix

source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer:
STANCE 22 - Disaggregated prefill/decode serving relocates the cost: on a Mooncake- or Dynamo-style deployment the redundant call is a KV-transfer problem.
Mechanism. Under prefill/decode disaggregation the extra agent turn does not just add tokens, it adds a scheduling event. The grown context must either be re-prefilled on a prefill worker and its KV blocks transferred to a decode worker over the interconnect, or served from a distributed KV store keyed on the prefix. The marginal cost of a redundant call is therefore a function of KV block reuse against that store plus interconnect bandwidth, not of token count alone.
Falsifiable hypothesis H22. With a prefix-addressed KV store in front of the prefill pool, the incremental cost of the redundant turn is sublinear in total context length because only the delta suffix is newly prefilled. If measured prefill GPU-seconds for the redundant turn scale linearly with full context length, the store is not being hit and H22 is refuted for this deployment.
Metrics. KV store hit rate at block granularity, bytes transferred per redundant turn, interconnect utilization during transfer, prefill worker queue depth, decode worker stall time waiting on KV arrival, and p95 TTFT decomposed into queue, prefill, transfer, and first-token components.
Controlled experiment. Fixed trajectory replay at fixed concurrency. Arm A redundant call present, Arm B elided, Arm C redundant call present with the KV store disabled. Arm C is the control that separates the store's contribution from the redundancy's contribution. Same weights, same seeds, same worker topology and pool sizes across arms.
Boundary conditions. The analysis only holds while the KV store's eviction policy retains the relevant prefix for the duration of an agent trajectory. Long agent sessions with high fleet churn will evict mid-trajectory and the cost profile reverts to full re-prefill. Report eviction events per trajectory.
Confounders. RDMA or NVLink transfer time is easily confused with prefill time if instrumentation only spans the request boundary; without per-phase spans the transfer cost is silently attributed to prefill. Network contention from unrelated tenants also inflates transfer time in a way that has nothing to do with redundancy.
Numbers. Sublinearity is an ESTIMATE that follows from block-level prefix reuse being possible in principle; it is not MEASURED here and depends entirely on this deployment's hit rate. Any bandwidth figure quoted without a link-level counter is not evidence.
Rollback. Not a production change, so the gate is on interpretation: if per-phase spans are unavailable, do not publish a cost attribution at all, because the prefill/transfer split cannot be recovered post hoc.
Scope. Deployment-architecture claim about where cost lands. It carries no implication about model capability.
risks: Per-phase spans are often missing, causing KV transfer time to be silently misattributed to prefill
KV store eviction mid-trajectory invalidates the sublinearity claim without any visible error
Cross-tenant network contention inflates transfer measurements independently of the behavior under study
evidence_required: Per-phase span traces separating queue, prefill, KV transfer, and first token
Block-granularity KV store hit rate and per-trajectory eviction counts
Link-level interconnect counters collected during the same window as the request traces

source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer:
STANCE 23 - Contrarian on the intervention target: fix the tool contract, not the agent, because a cheap idempotent tool makes redundancy harmless.
Mechanism. The premise that a redundant call must be suppressed assumes the call is expensive. A calculator is pure, deterministic, and microsecond-scale. If the tool layer memoizes on a normalized expression key, the second call returns from cache and the only residual cost is the extra decode turn. This converts a behavioral problem, which requires training or scaffolding changes, into a caching problem, which is one deployment away and carries no risk to model behavior.
Falsifiable hypothesis H23. After tool-side memoization, the remaining cost attributable to redundancy is entirely the extra decode turn, and total added latency per trajectory falls by the tool's own execution and network time. If added latency does not fall measurably, tool time was never a material fraction of the cost and the redundancy problem was mis-framed from the start.
Metrics. Tool cache hit rate, tool p50/p95 execution latency before and after, added decode turns per trajectory, end-to-end trajectory latency, and total tool invocations reaching the backend.
Controlled experiment. Deploy memoization behind a flag. Arm A flag off, Arm B flag on, same model weights, same prompts, same seeds, same eval set, interleaved by request so both arms see the same fleet conditions. Model behavior is unchanged by construction, which makes this a clean latency-only measurement.
Boundary conditions. Memoization is only safe for pure tools. A calculator qualifies. The moment the tool set includes anything with side effects, a clock, a random source, or external mutable state, blanket memoization is a correctness bug, not an optimization. The cache key must include every input that can affect the result, including precision and rounding mode.
Confounders. A tool cache warms over the eval run, so early requests in Arm B look like Arm A. Report the hit rate as a function of position in the run, or the aggregate understates the steady-state effect.
Numbers. No figure is MEASURED. The claim that calculator execution is microsecond-scale is an ESTIMATE based on it being a pure local computation with no I/O; if the deployed calculator is an RPC to a remote service, that estimate is wrong by orders of magnitude and must be replaced with a measured p50.
Rollback. Single config flag, disable on any correctness regression or any cache-key collision report. Collisions must be detectable, so log key and result hash for a sampled fraction.
Scope. Tool-layer engineering claim. It removes cost without changing the model, and therefore provides no evidence whatsoever about the model's abstention behavior.
risks: Blanket memoization is a correctness bug for any tool that is not pure
An incomplete cache key silently returns wrong results for precision- or mode-sensitive inputs
Cache warming during the eval run biases the aggregate hit rate downward
evidence_required: Measured tool p50/p95 execution latency, not an assumed one
Cache hit rate plotted against position in the run to show steady state
Sampled key/result-hash log demonstrating zero collisions over the eval window

source_user: An agent repeatedly calls a calculator when the answer is already known. Design metrics and an intervention. Scenario variant 196: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer:
STANCE 24 - The evaluation is underpowered: state the required sample size before running the arms, or the null result will be uninterpretable.
Mechanism. The proposed comparison is a paired difference in a proportion, final-answer correctness, plus a paired difference in a count, redundant calls per trajectory. Both are noisy at the item level. If the eval set is a few hundred items, the confidence interval on a correctness delta will comfortably straddle the decision threshold, and the experiment will conclude nothing while appearing to conclude safety.
Falsifiable hypothesis H24. The currently planned eval set cannot detect a 0.5 absolute point correctness change at conventional power. This is checkable directly: compute the paired standard error from a baseline run and compare the resulting minimum detectable effect against the decision threshold. If the minimum detectable effect is smaller than the threshold, H24 is refuted and the eval set is adequate.
Metrics. Item count, per-item paired variance of correctness, discordant-pair count for the paired test, minimum detectable effect at the chosen power, and the same quantities for redundant-call count.
Controlled experiment. This is a pre-experiment. Run the baseline arm twice with different seeds, treat the two runs as a null comparison, and measure the observed delta distribution. Any apparent effect in that null comparison is pure noise and sets the floor below which no arm difference is credible.
Boundary conditions. Paired analysis requires the two arms to see the same items, which fails if the intervention changes trajectory length enough to alter which items time out. Items that time out in one arm and not the other must be reported separately rather than dropped, since dropping them is a silent selection effect.
Confounders. Sampling temperature makes per-item outcomes stochastic even within an arm. Either fix the decode to greedy for the comparison, or run multiple samples per item and analyze at the item-mean level; mixing the two invalidates the variance estimate.
Numbers. The 0.5 point threshold is an ESTIMATE inherited from the intervention proposals, not a MEASURED quantity. The minimum detectable effect is computable and must be reported as MEASURED once a baseline run exists; until then no power claim should be made.
Rollback. The gate is on proceeding: if the null-comparison delta distribution has a spread comparable to the decision threshold, do not run the intervention arms until the eval set is enlarged or the decode is made deterministic.
Scope. Experimental-methodology claim. It constrains what any subsequent result can support and makes no claim about the model or the serving stack.
risks: A null result from an underpowered eval is routinely misread as evidence of safety
Timed-out items differ between arms and silently break the pairing if dropped
Sampling temperature inflates item-level variance and invalidates naive power calculations
evidence_required: Two-seed baseline null comparison with the observed delta distribution
Computed minimum detectable effect alongside the pre-registered decision threshold
Explicit accounting of items that completed in one arm but not the other

source_user: An agent repeatedly calls a calculator when the answer is already known. Design metrics and an intervention. Scenario variant 197: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer:
STANCE 25 - Attribute the behavior to the KV cache and attention over prior tool results: the model may not be attending to the result it already has.
Mechanism. A tool result sitting earlier in the context is only usable if attention actually routes to it at the decision step. In long agent trajectories the relevant result is buried under intervening reasoning and formatting tokens, and with any form of context compression, sliding window, or eviction-based KV management, it may not be in the cache at all. Under that reading the agent is not being wasteful, it is being correct given a context it can no longer see.
Falsifiable hypothesis H25. Redundancy rate increases monotonically with the token distance between the prior tool result and the decision point. If redundancy rate is flat across distance buckets, the mechanism is not retrieval failure and the fix should target the decision policy rather than context management.
Metrics. Redundancy rate bucketed by token distance to the prior matching result, fraction of decision steps where the prior result is outside the active KV window, and redundancy rate conditioned on whether any KV eviction or compression policy was active for that request.
Controlled experiment. Hold the model and prompt fixed and vary only the position of the prior tool result by injecting controlled amounts of neutral filler between the result and the decision point. Same weights, same seeds. Position becomes the sole manipulated variable, which is what makes the distance claim testable rather than correlational.
Boundary conditions. This only distinguishes retrieval failure from policy failure if the filler is genuinely neutral. Filler that changes topic or introduces new numbers is a confound, not a control. The manipulation also must not push the context past any length at which the serving stack changes strategy, or the arms differ in more than position.
Confounders. Long contexts co-vary with harder tasks in naturally collected data, so an observational distance effect may just be task difficulty. Only the injected-filler version breaks that tie.
Numbers. Monotonicity is an ESTIMATE of the expected shape, not a MEASURED curve. Any specific distance threshold quoted before running the filler experiment is unfounded.
Rollback. If the filler manipulation cannot be made topic-neutral to reviewer satisfaction, abandon this line rather than reporting the observational correlation as causal.
Scope. This is a claim about the interaction between context management and model behavior. A positive result would implicate the serving configuration, not the weights.
risks: Observational context-length effects are confounded with task difficulty
Non-neutral filler introduces the very information whose absence is being tested
Crossing a serving-stack length threshold makes the arms differ in more than position
evidence_required: Redundancy rate by injected-distance bucket from the controlled filler experiment
Per-request record of whether KV eviction or compression was active at the decision step
Reviewer-signed statement of filler neutrality with the filler text included

source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer:
STANCE 26 - Any training-side intervention must be gated on a loss-masking audit, because the wrong mask teaches the wrong lesson silently.
Mechanism. If the fix is trained rather than scaffolded, the training data contains assistant turns, tool-call turns, and tool-result turns. Tool results are environment output, not model output. If loss is computed over tool-result tokens the model is being trained to hallucinate tool outputs, which increases the probability of it fabricating a result instead of calling, a change that would look like a redundancy improvement while being a correctness catastrophe.
Falsifiable hypothesis H26. A run with tool-result tokens included in the loss will show reduced tool-call rate and increased fabricated-result rate relative to a correctly masked run. If fabricated-result rate is statistically indistinguishable between the two masking regimes, the masking choice is not the driver and H26 is refuted.
Metrics. Fraction of loss-bearing tokens by role, fabricated-result rate measured by comparing emitted result strings against the tool's actual return for the same input, tool-call rate, and final correctness. Fabricated-result rate is the primary endpoint.
Controlled experiment. Two runs, identical data, identical hyperparameters, identical seeds, differing only in the mask over tool-result spans. Because the mask is the only manipulated variable, any endpoint difference is attributable to it. Verify the mask by dumping the per-token loss weight vector for a sample of sequences before training starts.
Boundary conditions. The audit is only valid if the chat template used at training matches the one used at inference token for token. A template mismatch shifts role boundaries and the mask lands in the wrong place regardless of the masking code being correct.
Confounders. Reduced tool-call rate is the intended direction of the intervention, so it cannot by itself distinguish a good fix from a fabricating model. This is precisely why fabricated-result rate, not call rate, must be the primary endpoint.
Numbers. No rates are MEASURED here. The directional prediction is an ESTIMATE grounded in the mechanism that training on environment tokens makes the model model those tokens.
Rollback. Hard gate: no training-side fix ships without the per-token loss-weight dump and the fabricated-result comparison. If the dump is unavailable, the run is not evaluable and must be discarded rather than interpreted.
Scope. Training-methodology claim about how to avoid a specific silent failure. It is not a claim that the intervention works.
risks: Training on tool-result tokens teaches fabrication while superficially improving the target metric
A chat-template mismatch between training and inference misplaces the mask even when masking code is correct
Call-rate reduction alone cannot distinguish a correct fix from a fabricating model
evidence_required: Per-token loss-weight dump for sampled sequences from both masking regimes
Byte-level diff of the training-time and inference-time chat templates
Fabricated-result rate as the reported primary endpoint with its confidence interval

source_user: An agent repeatedly calls a calculator when the answer is already known. Design metrics and an intervention. Scenario variant 199: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer:
STANCE 27 - Operational safety framing: define the abort criteria and the blast radius before any arm reaches shared infrastructure.
Mechanism. Every proposed intervention, whether a logits processor, a scaffold change, a tool cache, or new weights, is a change to a system other people depend on. The failure mode that matters operationally is not that the fix underperforms, it is that the fix degrades an unrelated workload sharing the same GPUs, the same KV store, or the same tool backend, and that the degradation is attributed to something else.
Falsifiable hypothesis H27. Under a canary limited to a small traffic fraction, no unrelated workload's p95 latency degrades beyond its existing error budget. If any co-tenant p95 moves outside its budget during the canary window and the move correlates with canary traffic, H27 is refuted and the change must be reverted before expansion.
Metrics. Canary traffic fraction, per-tenant p95 latency and error rate, GPU memory headroom on affected nodes, tool backend queue depth, and a change-attribution marker on every canary request so co-tenant regressions can be correlated rather than guessed at.
Controlled experiment. Time-sliced canary: alternate the change on and off in fixed windows rather than running it continuously, so co-tenant metrics can be compared across on and off windows under otherwise identical fleet conditions. Continuous canaries confound the change with time-of-day load patterns.
Boundary conditions. This only works if co-tenant workloads are actually instrumented at p95 and if error budgets are written down in advance. Declaring the budget after seeing the numbers is not a safety process. The canary must also be revertible without a model reload, or the abort path is slower than the damage.
Confounders. Fleet-wide events, autoscaling, node draining, unrelated deploys, will produce co-tenant regressions during the window that have nothing to do with the change. The on/off alternation is what separates them.
Numbers. No thresholds are MEASURED. Any traffic fraction or budget quoted must come from the existing SLO document, and if no such document exists that absence is itself the finding to report.
Rollback. Automatic revert on any co-tenant budget breach correlated with on-windows, with revert executed by flag rather than redeploy. Time-to-revert must itself be measured during a rehearsal before the real canary.
Scope. Operational claim about deployment process. It says nothing about whether the intervention improves agent behavior, and a clean canary is not evidence of efficacy.
risks: Co-tenant degradation is routinely misattributed when canary requests are not marked
Error budgets defined after observing results are not a safety control
A revert path that requires a model reload is slower than the damage it is meant to contain
evidence_required: Pre-existing SLO document with per-tenant error budgets, dated before the canary
On/off time-sliced canary metrics with change-attribution markers on requests
Rehearsed time-to-revert measurement from a non-production drill

source_user: An agent repeatedly calls a calculator when the answer is already known. Design metrics and an intervention. Scenario variant 200: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer:
STANCE 28 - Segment by arithmetic difficulty: the aggregate redundancy rate is a mixture and the intervention should differ per segment.
Mechanism. Calling a calculator for a two-digit addition and calling it for a long division are different behaviors with different justifications. A model's internal arithmetic reliability degrades sharply with operand magnitude and operation type, so the correct abstention threshold is not a single number. An aggregate redundancy rate averages a segment where abstention is clearly right with a segment where calling is clearly right, and the mean describes neither.
Falsifiable hypothesis H28. Model arithmetic accuracy without tool access, measured per segment, will cross the accuracy of the tool-assisted path at some difficulty boundary, and redundant calls concentrated below that boundary are the only ones worth suppressing. If no-tool accuracy is flat across segments, the mixture argument fails and a single global threshold is defensible.
Metrics. Per-segment no-tool accuracy, per-segment tool-assisted accuracy, per-segment redundancy rate, and segment sizes. Segments defined a priori by operand digit count and operation class, published before any results are computed.
Controlled experiment. Two passes over a stratified eval set, tool access enabled and disabled, identical weights and seeds. The disabled pass measures the model's own arithmetic; the enabled pass measures the deployed behavior. The crossing point is read off the two per-segment curves.
Boundary conditions. Segment definitions must be fixed before the accuracy numbers are seen, or the boundary is fitted to noise. Segments must also be large enough individually to support an accuracy estimate; a segment with a handful of items produces a curve point with no meaning.
Confounders. Difficulty and formatting co-vary in most synthetic corpora, so a segment effect may be a template effect. Verify by checking that within-segment templates are heterogeneous.
Numbers. The existence of a crossing point is an ESTIMATE motivated by the general observation that language-model arithmetic reliability falls with operand size. No crossing location is MEASURED and none should be quoted until both curves exist.
Rollback. If any segment has too few items to support an estimate, report the curve with that point omitted and explicitly marked, rather than smoothing over it.
Scope. Evaluation-design claim about how to read the metric. It does not establish that any intervention works.
risks: Segments defined after seeing results fit the boundary to noise
Small segments produce meaningless curve points that still get plotted and quoted
Difficulty and prompt template co-vary in synthetic corpora, confounding the segment effect
evidence_required: Pre-registered segment definitions timestamped before results
Per-segment no-tool and tool-assisted accuracy curves with item counts and intervals
Within-segment template diversity audit

source_user: An agent repeatedly calls a calculator when the answer is already known. Design metrics and an intervention. Scenario variant 201: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer:
STANCE 29 - Treat the deliverable as a regression test, not a study: whatever is learned must be encoded as a gate that fails future runs.
Mechanism. A one-off study produces a number that decays. The durable artifact is an automated check in the eval harness that fails a build when redundancy rate exceeds a threshold on a frozen item set. This converts the finding into a constraint that future model versions, scaffold changes, and serving configuration changes must satisfy, which is the only mechanism by which the effort survives the next release.
Falsifiable hypothesis H29. A frozen-item redundancy gate will catch a deliberately regressed configuration. This is directly testable: introduce a known-bad configuration, one that removes the abstention instruction from the system prompt, and confirm the gate fails. If the gate passes a known-bad configuration, it does not measure what it claims and must be redesigned.
Metrics. Gate pass/fail, redundancy rate on the frozen set, false-failure rate measured across repeated runs of an unchanged configuration, and gate runtime, since a gate slower than the build will be disabled by whoever is on call.
Controlled experiment. Negative control by deliberate regression as above, plus a stability run of the unchanged configuration repeated enough times to estimate the false-failure rate under sampling noise. Both use identical weights and the frozen item set.
Boundary conditions. The frozen set will drift out of relevance as the agent's task distribution changes, so the gate needs an expiry date and a documented owner. An unowned gate that starts failing gets deleted rather than investigated, which is worse than having no gate.
Confounders. Sampling noise causes false failures; if the threshold is set at the observed mean the gate will fail roughly half the time on an unchanged system. The threshold must be set from the measured null distribution, not from the point estimate.
Numbers. No threshold is MEASURED yet. The threshold must be derived from the stability run and reported as MEASURED with its run count; any threshold chosen before that run is an ESTIMATE and must be labeled as one in the gate configuration itself.
Rollback. If false-failure rate exceeds a small pre-declared fraction, loosen the threshold or increase the frozen set rather than letting engineers learn to ignore the gate.
Scope. Engineering-process claim about durability of the finding. It is not evidence about model capability and a passing gate is not a capability claim.
risks: An unowned or expired gate gets deleted rather than investigated
Thresholds set at the point estimate produce ~50% false failures and train people to ignore the gate
A frozen item set silently stops representing the live task distribution
evidence_required: Negative-control run showing the gate fails a deliberately regressed configuration
Stability run with false-failure rate and the null distribution used to set the threshold
Gate ownership and expiry recorded in the harness configuration

source_user: An agent repeatedly calls a calculator when the answer is already known. Design metrics and an intervention. Scenario variant 202: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer:
STANCE 30 - Synthesis with an explicit falsification ladder: order the work so each rung can kill the next, and stop at the first rung that fails.
Mechanism. The proposals differ in cost by orders of magnitude, from a config flag to a training run. The correct structure is a ladder where each rung is cheap relative to the next and can refute the premise the next rung depends on. Rung 1: measure what redundancy costs in GPU-seconds and in user-visible latency. If it costs nothing measurable, stop; there is no problem. Rung 2: define and validate the oracle for 'already known', including inter-annotator agreement on a sample. If the oracle is not reliable, stop; no metric downstream is interpretable. Rung 3: establish statistical power against the decision threshold. If underpowered, enlarge the set before spending anything else. Rung 4: deploy the cheapest reversible fix, tool memoization or a scaffold-level abstention action, behind a flag with a canary. Rung 5: only if rungs 1 through 4 leave a material residual cost, consider a training-side fix, gated on the loss-masking audit and the fabricated-result endpoint.
Falsifiable hypothesis H30. The residual cost after rung 4 will be small enough that rung 5 is not economically justified. This is refuted if the measured post-rung-4 cost, in GPU-seconds and p95 latency, still exceeds the pre-declared materiality threshold.
Metrics. Per rung: the specific kill criterion, the cost in engineer-days and GPU-hours, and the decision taken. The ladder itself is the artifact and must be recorded with decisions and dates.
Controlled experiment. Each rung carries its own control as described in the preceding stances; the ladder adds the constraint that later rungs may not be started until the earlier rung's kill criterion has been evaluated and recorded in writing.
Boundary conditions. The ladder only works if the materiality threshold is declared before rung 1. Declared afterward, it will be set to whatever makes the already-preferred rung look justified.
Confounders. Organizational momentum. Once a training run is planned, rungs 1 through 3 tend to be executed as formalities. The written kill-criterion record with dates is the only defense.
Numbers. All costs must be tagged ESTIMATE at planning time and replaced by MEASURED values as each rung completes, with the estimate retained alongside so the estimation error is visible.
Rollback. Any rung that cannot produce its evidence artifact halts the ladder rather than being waived.
Scope. This is a plan for the system and the process. Nothing in it constitutes evidence about the model's domain capability, and every result it produces about the deployed agent must be reported as a system result.
risks: Kill criteria declared after the fact are set to justify the already-preferred option
Organizational momentum turns early cheap rungs into formalities that are executed but not heeded
Waiving a missing evidence artifact silently invalidates every downstream rung
evidence_required: Dated written record of each rung's kill criterion, evaluated before the next rung starts
Materiality threshold declared and timestamped before rung 1
Per-rung cost table retaining both the original ESTIMATE and the final MEASURED value
